description: Per (drug, event) biological plausibility ratings. Key format: '{drug_canonical}::{event_meddra_pt}' — lowercase canonical drug name from chembl_lookup.json, MedDRA Preferred Term in snake_case.
source_policy: HUMAN_CURATED -- rubric v1.1 (Bradford Hill) defined in prompts/plausibility_rubric.txt.

semaglutide::pancreatitis.rationale: GLP-1 receptor agonism directly stimulates pancreatic exocrine secretion and increases pancreatic ductal pressure in preclinical models. The link between this primary mechanism and pancreatitis is direct and requires no speculative inferential steps.

metformin::lactic_acidosis.rationale: Mitochondrial complex I inhibition directly impairs lactate oxidation in hepatocytes. In the presence of reduced renal clearance, metformin accumulation creates a direct, well-characterised pathway to lactic acidosis with no speculative steps required.

atorvastatin::common_cold.rationale: HMG-CoA reductase inhibition has no credible mechanistic pathway to rhinovirus susceptibility or upper respiratory tract immunity. No direct or indirect pharmacological basis connects cholesterol synthesis inhibition to viral respiratory infection.

montelukast::suicidal_ideation.rationale: CysLT1 receptor antagonism primarily targets peripheral airways, but leukotrienes have established roles in neuroinflammatory signalling. An indirect CNS pathway via leukotriene modulation of neuroinflammation and mood regulation is speculative but pharmacologically coherent under Bradford Hill criteria -- a mechanism can be reasonably hypothesised without being confirmed.

ciprofloxacin::tendon_rupture.rationale: While the primary MoA targets bacterial DNA gyrase and Topoisomerase IV, fluoroquinolones are known to exert off-target toxic effects on mammalian tenocytes, potentially via disruption of collagen synthesis and matrix metalloproteinase upregulation. This off-target pathway is indirect relative to the primary antibacterial MoA but is a pharmacologically coherent hypothesis.

pembrolizumab::pneumonitis.rationale: PD-1 inhibition directly removes negative regulatory checkpoints on T-cell activation, unleashing systemic immune responses. Autoimmune and inflammatory toxicities -- including pneumonitis -- are a direct, mechanistically inevitable consequence of this MoA and require no speculative inferential steps.

liraglutide::pancreatic_cancer.rationale: GLP-1 receptor agonism stimulates both exocrine and endocrine pancreatic function. Chronic receptor overstimulation as a speculative pathway to hyperplasia or neoplasia is pharmacologically coherent as an indirect hypothesis, though the link to carcinogenesis is not direct from the MoA text alone.

atorvastatin::dementia.rationale: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors reduce cholesterol synthesis systemically. Brain cholesterol is synthesised locally and is critical for neuronal membrane integrity, synaptic function, and myelination. Statins with CNS penetration could plausibly impair these processes indirectly, making dementia a pharmacologically speculative but non-arbitrary hypothesis.

albuterol::suicidal_ideation.rationale: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonism causes peripheral sympathetic activation. While primarily a pulmonary bronchodilator, adrenergic signalling has CNS effects via autonomic pathways and indirect neuroinflammatory or neuromodulatory routes. A speculative mechanistic link to complex psychiatric events like suicidal ideation is pharmacologically conceivable under Bradford Hill criteria, even without a confirmed pathway.
